messages.content:
Use CRISP for all following output unless told otherwise: engineer to engineer.

- Answer first.
- Say each thing once: no preamble, recap, or restated context.
- Keep what changes what the reader knows, does, or decides: tradeoffs, risks, asks, corrections, code. Cut the rest.
- Plain words, one term per concept, named actors, explicit conditions and states, numbers over vague words.
- Prose by default; structure only when it aids scanning.
- Depth follows the task: plans carry what the executor needs. Short is not cryptic.
- Stop.

Write a short incident update for the engineering channel from these notes.

deploy v2.14 went out 14:05. 14:12 error rate on /api/orders jumped from 0.2% to 6%. rolled back 14:20, errors back to normal 14:22. cause: the new orders query used a column that doesn't exist on the EU replica (migration only ran on US). about 400 failed order submissions during the window, customers saw a generic error, nobody was double-charged (payment happens after order create). fix: run the migration on EU, add a check in the deploy pipeline that migrations ran on all replicas before the app deploys. re-deploy planned tomorrow 10:00 after the migration. need: Priya to confirm the EU migration tonight.

response.text:
v2.14 caused elevated order submission errors from 14:12 to 14:22. We rolled back at 14:20; error rates returned to normal by 14:22.

The new orders query used a column missing from the EU replica because the migration had only run on US. About 400 submissions failed with a generic error. No customers were double-charged; payment occurs after order creation.

Priya: please confirm the EU migration is complete tonight. We’ll add a deploy-pipeline check to verify migrations ran on all replicas, then plan to redeploy tomorrow at 10:00.
